_readme: Every relic in the game. Edit this file, then run Prince's Palace > Build Default Content. id and displayName are always required. Everything else is optional and defaulted. RELICS ARE DRAFTED PER RUN: three are offered at the start of a descent, the player keeps one for that run only, and it is gone when the run ends. Nothing here is permanent progression. `rarity` is one of common, uncommon, rare, ultrarare, mythic, godlike (case-insensitive, default common) and is an AUTHORED statement about how often the relic should be offered -- unlike item rarity it is not derived from a tier, because a relic has no numbers to derive it from. Changing a relic's band is this one word and nothing else. `unlockedBy` names an AchievementIds value; empty means available from the very first run, and an unknown id is a content-build failure rather than a relic that silently never appears. `effect` names a PrincesPalace.Domain.Content.RelicEffect value (case-insensitive); OMIT IT for a relic that has no mechanic yet -- it resolves to None, which is exempt from the one-relic-per-effect rule precisely so a pool of named-but-unimplemented relics can exist. Every other effect must still be unique: two relics doing the same thing makes one of them a dead choice in a draft. iconPath is optional and points at Assets/_Project/Art/Items/Relics/Processed/ -- SceneBuilder.LoadSprite leaves the slot blank with a console warning until that file exists.
_placeholders: seven_teeth through drowned_lantern are DELIBERATELY MECHANIC-LESS. They exist so the draft, the rarity ladder and the glossary can be seen working against a pool big enough to be a real choice, before anybody has designed what they do. Give one an `effect` when it earns one; until then they are honest about being furniture.

relics.description: Whenever this character attacks, they strike the same target a second time.
After casting, the next hit this character takes is reduced by half.
Killing an enemy grants this character another turn.

A jawbone worn smooth by counting. Every kill is a line struck off, and every line is worth something.

Mechanic: killing an enemy pays gold equal to about 30% of its own experience reward (minimum 1 gold).

Every debt the sea remembers, written small. Swing, and a line of it is struck out - whatever you are waiting on comes back a turn sooner.

Mechanic: every attack you land reduces all of your active cooldowns by 1 turn.

Too heavy for the finger it was made for, so somebody wore it around their throat instead. The closer it sits to your last breath, the sharper it bites on your behalf.

Mechanic: the lower your health, the harder and faster you fight - up to +30% damage and +20% speed at 25% health or below, scaling smoothly in between.

Paper thin, and it flakes - but it draws hard and fast, and what it gives back does not last.

Mechanic: casting a spell grants +20% speed for your next turn.

Dented on the inside only, from a foot that never stopped moving. Every swing wears them in a little more, up to a point.

Mechanic: each attack you land permanently speeds you up by 10% for the rest of the fight, up to +40% total.

It has been counting since before you found it, and every third blow it lets you in on the tally.

Mechanic: every third attack you land this fight deals 40% bonus damage.

Still lit, which is the troubling part. Whatever a spell touches, it marks - and the next blow that lands there burns brighter for it.

Mechanic: a spell that lands marks its target; your next attack against a marked target deals 50% bonus damage.
Taken from the thing that guards the first wood. It has no power yet.
Strikes 20% harder, and bruises just as easily.

It drinks a little from every spell and gives the fourth one back with interest. The interest is reckoned on the spell itself, never on whatever else was helping.

Mechanic: every fourth spell you cast this fight deals 50% bonus damage.

Small, dented, and held by somebody who lived. It turns a blow and a curse with the same indifference.

Mechanic: +25 physical resistance and +25 magical resistance.

Small enough to carry, sharp enough to matter. Whatever a spell touches, the box opens on its own and finishes the thought.

Mechanic: landing a spell on an enemy immediately follows with a free basic attack against them.

Fifty-two ways for a fight to go your way, and it never shows you which one until the card is already turned.

Mechanic: every landed attack rolls one of three outcomes at random - heal 5% health and 10% mana, splash 25% of the damage onto every other enemy, or slow the target by 30% speed for a turn.

The oldest word for fire, cut so deep the stone still says it twice. Every spell it hears, it repeats.

Mechanic: a single-target damaging spell you cast repeats itself once more on the same target, for free.
